title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

chapters.title: How you fall
chapters.teaser: Fast, slow, sideways or all at once. The way your soul actually falls for someone.

chapters.title: Your flirting style
chapters.teaser: What you think you're doing, what they think you're doing, and the one move that lands.

chapters.title: Your attachment pattern
chapters.teaser: Clingy, cool, steady or somewhere in between. How you hold on when you care.

chapters.title: Jealousy and your trigger
chapters.teaser: The exact thing that sets you off, and what you do instead of saying it.

chapters.title: Yeon's red flag report
chapters.teaser: The love habit you keep repeating. Yeon does not soften this chapter.

chapters.title: What you actually need
chapters.teaser: Not your type. Your match. The kind of person and love that lets you relax.

text.how-you-fall: You fall slowly and then completely. Jeong is the candle, and candles don't light up a stadium, they light up a face across a small table. You need a real conversation, the kind that goes past midnight and somehow turns into talking about your childhood, before anything in you moves. Once it does, you feel it intensely. You remember everything: the song playing when they first held your hand, the exact phrasing of their text. Your love is intimate, observant and deeply personal. People who are loved by you feel understood in a way they rarely have before. The risk is that you can fall for the inner world you've imagined in someone, filling silences with meaning they didn't intend. Check in with the real person, not just the beautiful version in your head.
text.flirting: Your flirting is quiet and devastating. You don't make a show. You listen, you notice, and then you say something so specific that the other person feels like you've read their diary. "You go quiet when people talk about your dad." A little risky, very effective. You flirt through attention and meaning: a song you send at 11pm, a book you think they'd like, a thoughtful question nobody else asked. With people you're not into, you're warm but polite. With someone you like, the warmth gets focused like a flame. The challenge is that it can be so subtle they miss it entirely. Add one obvious signal. Hold eye contact a second longer. Say "I like talking to you." Candles are allowed to flicker on purpose.
text.attachment: Your pattern runs warm and anxious when you love deeply. You're emotionally tuned in, which means you also pick up every tiny shift, real or imagined. A cooler goodnight can keep you awake. You may replay conversations and draft replies in your head long before you send anything. You give a lot of care, often more than you ask for, and then quietly feel hurt when it isn't returned in the same careful way. When you feel safe, you are tender, loyal and wonderfully devoted. The work is learning to ask instead of interpret. Your intuition is strong, but it isn't a mind-reading license. "Hey, you seemed off tonight, are we okay?" will save you three days of quiet spiraling.
text.jealousy: Your jealousy is private and it burns low and long. You won't cause a scene. You'll go a little quiet, a little formal, and then lie awake replaying the moment they laughed at someone else's story. Your trigger is emotional intimacy. Physical attractiveness in others bothers you less than the idea that someone else gets the deep, real version of your person. If they confide in a friend before you, that stings more than any flirt ever could. Because you're so perceptive, you're sometimes right, and that makes the jealousy feel justified even when it isn't. Try separating facts from stories. Write down what actually happened, then what you're afraid it means. Usually the second list is much longer, and much less true.
text.red-flag: Yeon, unfiltered: you keep a scrapbook of hurts. You forgive out loud, then quietly remember every forgotten anniversary, every careless word, every time you felt second. One day it all comes out at once and your partner is blindsided by a list they didn't know existed. Second flag: the silent test. You'll wait to see if they notice you're upset instead of telling them, and when they don't, it becomes proof they don't really care. Nobody passes a test they don't know they're taking. Third: you can romanticize people who are emotionally unavailable, because their mystery gives your imagination room to work. Light your candle for someone who sits close to it, not someone who stays in the doorway.
text.what-you-need: You need emotional presence. A partner who talks about feelings without making it weird, who remembers what matters to you, and who reassures you without needing to be asked every time. You need depth over noise. Big parties and constant plans can tire you out, while a quiet evening cooking together and talking can refill you for a week. You also need someone steady enough that your sensitivity has a safe place to land, and who won't use it against you in a fight. Above all, you need consistency. Not grand gestures, just the same warmth on an ordinary Wednesday as on your birthday. With the right person you burn beautifully for years, a small steady flame that never needs to compete with the sun.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, you love like candlelight. Close, warm, and so attentive it feels like being read.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And you remember every single thing they did wrong. With dates.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: That's just how deeply you care! You notice everything.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also give silent tests. They failed the one they didn't know they were taking.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Ask instead of guessing. "Are we okay?" is a beautiful sentence.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Your intuition is strong. It is not a lie detector. Use your words.

spring.intro: With Wood in command and Wood feeding Fire, a spring-born Jeong Fire is a lamp with plenty of oil. Your love is focused and devoted: you choose one person and illuminate every detail of them. You remember the song from the first date and the name of their childhood dog. That attention makes people feel deeply seen. With so much support behind your flame, the risk is intensity. You can analyze a relationship until it becomes a project, reading meaning into every pause. Earth, your output, is the cure here: practical rituals, shared routines, something you build together rather than examine. Let the candle light the room instead of scorching one spot.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Jeong, you reread their text eleven times. It said 'ok'. It means ok.

summer.intro: In summer, Fire is everywhere, so a summer-born Jeong Fire is a candle burning at noon. You have plenty of heat, but you constantly compare your glow with the bigger lights around you. In love, that shows up as a quiet competitiveness. You notice who your partner laughs with, who texts them, who they follow. It is not jealousy exactly, more a worry about fading into the brightness. Same-element Fire is a rival as well as a friend in saju. Water and Earth calm you: a steady partner who chooses you plainly and does not play games. Your light is not smaller. It is closer, and close light is the one people read by.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Jeong, you don't have to outshine the room. You're the light they read by.

autumn.intro: Autumn is Metal's season, and Fire controls Metal. A candle in autumn is the smith's flame, steadily shaping something precious, so an autumn-born Jeong lover works carefully on what they love. You are the person who refines a relationship: talking through conflict, remembering what went wrong last time, adjusting. That commitment is rare and lovely. It is also tiring, because you are spending your heat on improving someone else. Wood is what feeds you, and in romance that means admiration, curiosity about your inner world, someone who asks you questions back. You do not need a project partner. You need someone who wants to know what you are thinking at 2am.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Jeong, they're a person, not a renovation. Stop sanding their edges and let them love you.

winter.intro: Water commands winter, and Water controls Fire. Born in winter, a Jeong Fire is the candle in a cold window: small, steady and the most welcome thing on the street. You love quietly and loyally, and you guard your flame because you know how easily it can be blown out. In romance that means slow trust. You may test someone with small disclosures before you let them see the real warmth. When they pass, your devotion is extraordinary. When they fail, you close the shutters without a word. Wood, your resource, looks like a partner who is consistent and encouraging. Choose someone who cups their hands around the flame instead of breathing on it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Jeong, the right person will shelter your little flame. You don't have to hide it.

earth.intro: Earth days are the last weeks of a season, and you were born in them, Jeong. A candle in a clay room, warming the space it's in. You love quietly and thoroughly: the remembered detail, the right song, the safe evening. Fire feeds Earth, so much of your care disappears into making things comfortable, and you rarely ask for credit. The risk is that your person never sees how much you're doing. You need someone who notices small warmth and names it. Show them where to look.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Jeong, subtle is lovely. Too subtle is invisible.

strength.strong: A strong Jeong Fire is a lamp turned up high. With plenty of Fire and Wood behind you, your love is focused, passionate and occasionally scorching. You notice everything about your person, and you expect the same attention back. Your blind spot is intensity that tips into control: probing questions, needing to know where they are, analyzing moods until they feel examined. Your devotion is a gift, but it can feel like an interrogation lamp. Turn it down a notch. Trust the quiet days. Let them keep a few private corners. A candle lights the whole room best when it is not held too close.
strength.weak: A weak Jeong Fire is a small flame in a drafty room. With little support in your chart, you love deeply but guard yourself constantly. You may give endless attention to a partner while hiding your own needs, worried that asking will blow the flame out. Your blind spot is shrinking to protect the connection: going along, staying agreeable, absorbing hurt quietly. Then one day you simply go cold, and they never saw it coming. Say small truths early, while they are still small. The right person shelters your flame. The wrong one makes keeping it lit feel like your job alone.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood in your chart turns love into a growth plan. You want things to move forward, define the relationship, make progress, and slow phases make you restless. You can also be stubborn in arguments, holding your position like a tree in wind. In love this looks like big intentions and a little impatience. Balance it with Metal energy: clear agreements, pruning what isn't working, and accepting that some things are already finished growing. Not every relationship needs to become a forest. Some are perfect as a single, steady tree.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means beginnings are your hard part. You might hold back until someone else makes the first move, define things, or suggest the next step, and you can stay in a comfortable but stuck situation for too long. Your love is real, it just doesn't push. Balance it by practicing small starts: suggest the date, send the first text, say what you hope for out loud. Green things help as reminders, a plant by your bed, a green phone case. Love grows when someone plants it. Sometimes that someone is you.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your love bright, fast and a little combustible. You fall hard and feel everything at full volume, whether you show it out loud or keep it behind your eyes. The highs are glorious. The lows, when attention drops, feel like the lights went out. You can also lose interest once the excitement settles. Balance it with Water energy: slowing down, letting quiet evenings count, and sitting with feelings before reacting. Ask yourself if you love the person or the thrill. The best flame for you burns steady, not just bright.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means passion and visibility don't come easily in love. You might care deeply but struggle to show it, hold back affection until you're sure, or feel awkward with romantic gestures. People can mistake your reserve for disinterest. Balance it by letting warmth out in small, brave doses: a compliment, a hug that lasts a second longer, a little playfulness. Warm colors and sunlight help you feel more expressive. You don't need fireworks. You just need people to see that the light is on.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth makes you a steady, devoted partner who can get a little stuck. You value security, routine and loyalty, and you might stay in familiar patterns even when they've stopped making you happy. Change feels risky. You may also over-care, taking on your partner's problems as your own. Balance it with Wood energy: try something new together, plan an adventure, let the relationship grow in surprising directions. Safe is wonderful. Safe and alive is even better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means love can feel unsteady. You might worry about where things stand, struggle to settle into commitment, or jump between highs and lows. You can also find it hard to trust that someone will stay. Balance it by building small, reliable rituals: a weekly date, a regular call, a shared routine. Choose partners who are consistent rather than exciting. Earth tones and home-cooked meals help you feel grounded. Stability isn't boring. For you, it's what lets love feel safe enough to enjoy.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives you strong standards and very clear boundaries in love. You know what you want and what you won't tolerate, which is healthy, until it becomes rigid. You can be critical, quick to judge, or end things abruptly when disappointed. Balance it with Fire energy: warmth, forgiveness, play. Let small mistakes be small. Say the kind thing before the honest thing. Strong boundaries keep you safe. Soft edges let people actually come close enough to love you.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are your hard part in love. You might say yes when you mean no, stay too long, or let people treat you less well than you deserve because you don't want conflict. Your heart is open, sometimes too open. Balance it by practicing clear, simple limits: "I'm not okay with that," without a long explanation. Decluttering and white or silver accents can help you feel sharper. Boundaries aren't walls. They're the frame that makes the picture of your love clear.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water makes your love deep, intuitive and sometimes overwhelming. You feel everything, read every mood and can get lost in emotional currents or imagined stories. You may also avoid commitment, drifting rather than choosing. Balance it with Earth energy: grounding conversations, practical plans, partners who are steady and clear. Write down what actually happened before reacting to what you feel happened. Your depth is beautiful. It just needs a shore so you don't get swept away.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means emotional depth and rest don't come easily in love. You might stay busy, keep conversations practical, or struggle to sit with vulnerable feelings, yours or your partner's. Love can feel like a to-do list. Balance it with slow, quiet moments: late talks, journaling, listening without fixing. Navy and black, water by your bed, and slow evenings help you soften. You don't need to drown in feelings. Just let yourself wade in a little deeper.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you want it defined, labeled and growing by Thursday. Breathe.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your hope is beautiful. Let it grow at the speed of a real person.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: you fall hard and fast, out loud or in silence. Then the second act bores you.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is a gift. Let it simmer a while. Slow love tastes better.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: staying somewhere stale because leaving takes effort isn't loyalty. It's inertia.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Make sure it's going somewhere that still feeds you.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: your dating checklist has forty points. Nobody passes. Including you.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Standards protect you. Leave one door open for someone surprising.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: you wrote a whole love story in your head. They've read none of it.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is gorgeous. Share a little of it with the real person.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Love won't start itself. Send the first text. Plant something.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Waiting for them to make the move isn't patience. It's hiding behind a nice word.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? Your love is real, it just whispers. Let someone hear it.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: A compliment you only think doesn't count. Say it, then survive the blushing.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? You love brightly but drift. A small weekly ritual keeps you anchored.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Three crushes, zero follow-through. Pick one and show up twice in a row.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? Your kindness needs a boundary. A no keeps your yes worth something.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Three cancellations and a fourth chance isn't generosity. It's a pattern you're funding.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? You act before you feel. Pause and ask what you actually want.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Over someone in a weekend isn't healing. It's skipping the chapter. Read it.
